targets.authors: Naftulin, D., Ware, J., & Donnelly, F.
targets.title: The Doctor Fox lecture: A paradigm of educational seduction.
targets.evidence_quote:
In an attempt to formulate an alternative explanation
of the findings, we replicated the 1973 study, using the original video of the lecture and following the
exact methodology of the original study.
targets.outcome_quote:
We found that the 1973 results were consistently replicated, and
the Dr. Fox effect (as defined and measured by the original
researchers) stands empirically as a solid effect even after 40 years,
despite the old-fashioned movie of the lecture and the shift to a
population of college students. However, we also found that the
critical flaw of the research was at the level of the conceptual
conclusions. Naftulin et al. (1973) interpreted their findings erroneously, thereby misleading generations of researchers and academicians.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original positive ratings were reproduced consistently, but the main message is that those ratings do not validly establish illusory learning or educational seduction.
